consequence_notes: Under a worse-case variation of this same event (occupants not restrained, vehicle rolling/overturning completely rather than settling front-down, greater excavation depth, or structural cabin failure on impact), this could plausibly have resulted in severe crush injuries, ejection trauma, or fatality — this is a hazard category with an inherently high severity ceiling
barrier_notes: seatbelt use and complete PPE compliance by all occupants are explicitly confirmed, and these controls appear to have been directly responsible for the absence of a severe injury outcome despite the high-energy nature of the event; however, the underlying engineering/procedural controls that failed to prevent the vehicle from sliding into the excavation in the first place (e.g., barricading/delineation of the excavated area, ramp surface condition, edge protection near excavations) represent a clear gap
exposure_notes: Vehicle occupant(s) inside the cabin throughout the loss-of-control event, the slide, and the impact/settling at the bottom of the excavation; direct exposure to deceleration forces, potential cabin intrusion, and the vehicle's final unstable resting position (front-down)
